items.label: A
items.critique: A gatekeeper's argument laid out cleanly: problem, tally ('Three wagons robbed this month!'), condition, reward. 'Is [Person] still breathing? Then the gate stays shut!' is a crafted reminder; too well built for Nox.

items.label: B
items.critique: 'Too many prying eyes the closer we get by air', 'Forest beasts will heed its bite', 'Go! Don't just stand there.' Slightly odd phrasing and a terse, practical send-off are the campaign's opening.

items.label: C
items.critique: 'valiant [Class] of [Place]! We've been expecting you!', 'located East of here', 'I should be in my house at the center of town' and 'nettlesome urchins'. Instructional, a little stiff, true Westwood.

items.label: D
items.critique: Opens on a confession ('Don't look at me like that. I know! It's our fault.') and 'it never asked for wages' irony. Character-driven framing and tight structure read as new.

items.label: E
items.critique: 'Traitors! Traitors inside our own walls!' and 'You, however, are no man of mine.' A polished political setup with a neat road-opening reward; more literary than Nox's openings.

items.label: F
items.critique: Dry academic understatement ('a most unfortunate hour', 'not some petty Imp', 'squats in my tower. Do hurry.'). Elegant, but the irony is not Westwood's tone.

items.label: G
items.critique: 'A Lich! In my mine!' and 'Bones in my tunnels and a Lich in my vein!' are crafted comic exasperation, and it follows the same closed-road-until-monster-dies template as A, D and F.

items.label: H
items.critique: 'Something is deeply amiss in our land', 'the recent surge of violence in the local creatures', supplies and gold, 'Go to the shop'. Plain, tutorial-like, slightly bureaucratic; a campaign start.

items.label: I
items.critique: 'Wildlife incursions in the settled areas is on a steady rise' (a grammar slip), 'antiquated records', a blank page break and a reminder naming the book and amulet. Wordy, tutorial exposition; unmistakably Westwood.

items.label: J
items.critique: 'We have arrived, lad.', 'timeless fortress home', 'Training grounds of the glorious [Class]!', 'It weeds out the weak recruits.' Short, grand and plain; the campaign's voice.

tells: The new openings share one template: a place-keeper says the road or gate is shut until a monster or villain is removed, then offers passage as the reward. Westwood's openings are mentor send-offs or tutorial errands with practical directions.

Westwood's openings are instructional and spatial ('located East of here', 'Go to the shop', 'The road across these bridges', 'Follow the tunnel'); the new ones spend their words on the speaker's character and situation.

The new reminders are crafted comic lines that echo the opening ('Is [Person] still breathing?', 'Bones in my tunnels...'); Westwood's reminders are generic nudges ('Get a move on', 'You need to press on now, lad').

Westwood uses grand stock phrases and slight grammatical slips ('deeply amiss', 'timeless fortress home', 'incursions ... is on a steady rise'); the new texts are grammatically clean and use understatement and irony.
Westwood's speakers call the player 'lad' or by [Class]; the new ones use 'brave Adventurer' or no address at all and instead offer a personal confession or exasperation.
